answer: No. Your records show lisinopril 10 mg was stopped on September 22, 2025. Dr. Elena Marsh stopped it because of a dry cough and switched you to losartan 50 mg daily. At your December 2025 visit the cough had resolved. Lisinopril is also on your allergy/intolerance list for that cough. The app that still lists it is most likely showing an old entry (one Kestrel Harbor Hospital-sourced record still shows it as active). Please ask the app to remove it, and do not restart it. Lisinopril and losartan are in related drug families, so taking both would not be appropriate. One more thing to raise with your doctor: the hospital stopped hydrochlorothiazide on March 5, 2026 because of low sodium, but your clinic's records and some lists still show it as active, and your sodium was still slightly low (134) in June 2026. Please ask Dr. Marsh to confirm whether you should be taking it. My records can't settle that.
short: Lisinopril was stopped on 2025-09-22 for a dry cough and replaced by losartan 50 mg daily; it should not be taken. Separately, please confirm with the doctor whether hydrochlorothiazide (stopped by the hospital in March 2026 for low sodium) is meant to be continued.
